newsitem.title: USA: California's unemployment rate drops to 6.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: California's unemployment rate drops to 6.2 pct.

text.p: California's unemployment rate dropped to 6.2 percent in June from a revised 6.4 percent in May in a sign the state's economic expansion remained on track, the state said on Friday.

June's 6.2 percent rate was the lowest unemployment rate in the state since September 1990. The unemployment rate a year ago, in June 1996, was 7.2 percent, the Employment Development Department said.
June also marked the 20th consecutive month of record high payroll employment. The state added 20,100 additional jobs over the month, the department said.
The number of people employed in California was 14,840,000 in June.
Six industry sectors added jobs over the month, gaining 24,200 positions, while three industry divisions reported job declines amounting to a loss of 4,100.

Most of the job growth was in the services sector, up 15,600 jobs. Growth in business services, amusement and recreation services, and health services offset the seasonal decline in private educational services, the department said.
Other industry divisions showing job growth over the month were manufacturing, up 3,200 jobs, and retail and wholesale trade, up 2,500 jobs, the department said.
The number of people employed in agriculture was 390,000 in June, down 2,700 jobs over the month but up 14,900 jobs over the year.
